title: On the definition of toxicity in NLP
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not conduct a benchmark measurement itself but identifies religious bias as a significant problem in existing toxicity datasets and detection models. It argues that current ill-defined approaches to toxicity detection cause this bias.
findings: The paper asserts that current, ill-defined approaches to toxicity detection cause religious bias in datasets, contributing to flawed models. It does not present new data on this topic but cites existing research to highlight it as a known problem that its proposed stress-level-based definition of toxicity aims to address.
